card.title: Growing and decaying current in LR circuits

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: An LR current grows as I_0 (1 − e^(−Rt/L)) toward V/R and decays as I_0 e^(−Rt/L) toward zero. The time constant is L/R. The inductor stops the current from jumping, and the stored energy returns as heat during decay.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Governing equation for "Growing and decaying current in LR circuits" — state with units, then use in one numerical.
Growth: I = I_0 (1 − e^(−Rt/L))
Decay: I = I_0 e^(−Rt/L)

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: ❌ state the rule without its limit → ✅ note when it applies / stops applying.  ·  ❌ no diagram → ✅ add one labelled figure / structured list.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: 63% on the way up, 37% left on the way down, after one τ.  ·  e^(−1) ≈ 0.37.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: When a battery is connected to a resistor and an inductor in series, the current starts at zero and rises toward I_0 = V/R. The self-induced emf opposes the rise, so the rise is gradual.  ·  The growth equation is I = I_0 (1 − e^(−Rt/L)). At t = 0, I = 0. After a long time the exponential vanishes and I = I_0.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Covers only: growing, decaying current in lr circuits (within Electromagnetic Induction).  ·  Out of scope here: topics of neighbouring units in Physics — don't mix them.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Current cannot jump in an inductor.  ·  Growth is toward V/R.  ·  Decay is toward zero after the battery is removed.  ·  The time constant is L/R.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: If the battery is then removed and the coil is left connected across the resistor, the current decays as I = I_0 e^(−Rt/L). It starts at I_0 and falls toward zero.  ·  The time constant τ = L/R is the time for the growth to reach about 63% of I_0, because 1 − e^(−1) is about 0.63. In decay, one time constant leaves about 37% of the current.  ·  A large L or a small R makes the change slow. The inductor behaves as an open circuit at the first instant and as a wire after a long time, for a steady battery.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: τ = L/R  ·  The current does not jump to V/R.  ·  Growth and decay use different formulas.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: τ = L/R, not R/L.  ·  After a long time a pure inductor on DC has no voltage.  ·  Say growth or decay before writing the formula.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: I_0 is V/R, not V/L.  ·  Write Growth: I = I_0 (1 − e^(−Rt/L)) and say what each symbol means.  ·  Mark the known values, then substitute one step at a time.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Finish with the number, the unit, and the direction when the quantity has one.  ·  State the limit / condition where a formula or rule stops being valid before applying it.  ·  Energy (1/2) L I^2 builds during growth and returns as heat in the resistor during decay. The spark when a large inductor is switched is that energy.
